Subject: Re: Production degradation Mar 8-9 — provisional root cause and remediation ETA

Quick technical summary from investigation so far:
- Root cause (provisional): a hot-shard condition combined with a mis-sized inference batch window under a bursty traffic pattern. At p99, memory pressure caused backpressure and transient failures; a small kernel path returned 5xx for overloaded workers.
- Evidence: kernel crash traces + KV cache thrash in the logs provided (attached). We're confident this is an execution-path stress issue rather than model corruption.

Mitigation plan & ETA:
1) Immediate: roll configuration change to reduce max batch coalescing and enable an extra pre-warm worker set — estimated 2-4 hours to deploy and verify.
2) Near-term: deploy a patch that improves shard distribution and adds circuit-breaker for the kernel path — ETA 72 hours (testing in staging now).
3) Preventative: scheduling change and new monitoring for p99 and 5xx spikes, plus a playbook for automatic worker pre-warm.

Impact on commercial ask: I recommend we offer a provisional credit to acknowledge business impact while we complete the remediation. From an ops standpoint we will have the immediate mitigation ready to push as soon as I get sign-off.

Attachments: [engineer-notes-kv-trace.txt] (internal)

--
Ben Carter
Staff Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
